canonical_definition: Causal Reasoning is the ability to discern cause-effect relationships by comprehending context and answering causality queries consistent with causal laws, often operationalized as identifying plausible causal links (e.g., "Cause/Caused by" relations) or assembling causal chains to address why-questions. Some definitions extend this to include reasoning with interventions and counterfactuals (per Pearl’s hierarchy), estimating interventional distributions (e.g., P(E2|do(E1))), or maintaining correct causal ordering of actions in planning contexts. It is broadly framed as a core feature of intelligence for understanding world mechanics, applied across domains like dynamic visual scenes, anomaly detection, and multi-hop question answering.
